search_method: Bounded format-specific comparison of four named C++ XML parser libraries; exact Debian binary-package and Homebrew formula lookups, all hits recorded in registry-snapshot.json
ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the library's -dev package(s) (by_inst)
selection: Four verified C++ XML packages ranked by Debian -dev package installs: Xerces-C++ 2,676, pugixml 1,503, TinyXML2 487, libxml++ 275 (three ABI packages; ABI-5 alone has seven). libxml++ shares the libxml2 C parser family and is not an independent engine.
uncertainty: All four C++ XML paths pass the namespace-aware catalog control with source coverage and AFL++ feedback. Xerces-C++, pugixml and libxml++ pass the shared second valid control; TinyXML2 uses a no-processing-instruction variant because it rejects that instruction. libxml++ parser-only feedback and native libxml2 parser.c lines are repeatable and input-dependent. The bounded search covered four named format-specific libraries, so other C++ XML packages remain unmeasured. Homebrew install-on-request orders the first three differently and its libxml++ formula is an older ABI. The libxml++ 275 Debian dev installs sum three ABIs, while its matching ABI-5 package has seven. Two small valid UTF-8 controls cannot establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, encoding or malformed-input behavior.
